producer: Media Exchange Server (Go) of Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows, cmd/exchange-vectors
notes: Every transcript was produced by the real exchange server (engine, directory, accounts, relay, cast table) over TLS on loopback, with one injected clock instant, seeded id and token sources and a third-party port pool whose binds are not sockets. The bytes are a function of the code and nothing else.

A step is one frame as it crossed the stream above TLS: `json` is the body, `hex` is the whole frame (the 4-byte big-endian length, then the body). A frame is recorded when the script reads or writes it, in the order of the script.

A client replays a transcript by encoding every client->server step to exactly its `hex` and decoding every server->client step to the same values. Ids, tokens and codes are the scenario's; a client under test supplies its own ids and compares the rest.

After `connected` and after `upload-accepted` the bytes are not envelopes: tunnels are recorded up to `connected` and never beyond; an upload continues as `chunk` steps (a 4-byte length counting the flag byte plus the payload, the flag byte, the payload) and the listener's HTTP exchange is an `http` step.

`chunks` lists every flag combination of the two defined bits, a zero length (the clean end of a broadcast) and the chunks that close a stream (an undefined flag bit, a length above 1048576, the largest length word); a chunk of exactly 1048576 bytes of length is the largest accepted and is not listed because of its size.

The frame limit is 16384 bytes of JSON until a stream is authenticated (up to and including welcome or enrolled) and 262144 after it, both ways; a record is at most 16384 bytes of JSON as a reader receives it, the members the server adds included (item BS).

Reasons: bad-credentials, device-revoked, version-unsupported, tls-required, id-collision, capacity, port-unavailable, unavailable and rate-limited are produced in the `refusals` transcript (with limit-reached and protection-unsupported); invitation-invalid, login-taken, password-policy, limit-reached (the cap on accounts) and not-permitted are produced in `registration`, signed-out in `password`, and rate-limited by the pace of password checks in `pace`. The refusal that answers a schemaVersion 1 frame carries schemaVersion 2.

`limit-reached` is a count limit of the server or of the account (resources, broadcasts, devices, accounts); `capacity` is the server unable to take more - a record or a frame over its size, the work queue of the password hash full, no room for another pairing code. A client that retries later is right for the second and wrong for the first.

Registration (`register`) carries an invitation by `invitation` (one-time) or `invitationPassword` (the shared invitation password), exactly one of them: the names of DEVICE-EXCHANGE item AQ, which every `register` step of this corpus uses. The server also reads the names it first used, `invitationCode` and `sharedPassword`, and no step uses them. `enrolled` carries `accountKind` (`member` or `guest`).

`limit-reached` is a count limit of the server or of the account (resources, broadcasts, devices, accounts, and the clipboard's `clipboardBytes`); `capacity` is the server unable to take more - a record or a frame over its size, the work queue of the password hash full, no room for another pairing code, the account's second overlapping clipboard put. A client that retries later is right for the second and wrong for the first.

The `clipboard` transcript is section 22 (ticket 229): after `clipboard-ready` and after the members of `clipboard-value` the bytes are RAW - one step per byte run, whose `hex` is the bytes exactly as they crossed the stream; a frame assembler stops there. A put's completion is judged against a short probe for bytes beyond the declared size, and a sender that half-closes is judged at once.

This corpus is evidence for sections 5 to 7, 22 and 27 at edition 1.1. The transcripts `sealed-devices`, `sealed-folder`, `sealed-grant` and `sealed-clipboard` run against a server that advertises `sealed` (item DP); every other transcript runs against one that does not, so its `welcome.features` carries no `sealed` and its clipboard kinds are `text`, `image` and `file`.

The `sealed` member of this file lists every box of the `sealed-*` transcripts with the context it was sealed under, the devices it is from and to, and the clear payload it opens to. The server did not make, open or check a box (item DH): the boxes are sealed by the generator over the fixed device keys of the shared vector file e2e-v1.json, so a product that holds that file's private keys opens every one of them. See `sealed.notes`.

The transcripts `admin-native` and `admin-websocket` are evidence for remote administration (ticket 245, DEVICE-EXCHANGE 1.4, REMOTE-ADMIN.md and WEB-BINDING.md). `admin-native` exercises the length-prefixed envelope stream inside TLS (0x00), including admin-disabled, allowedAddresses exclusion, wrong password, rate-limited by the per-address pacer, capacity, lapsed session token, and all 18 carried operations with exact reply shapes and connectionString on invitation.create; `admin-websocket` exercises the WebSocket opening (/v2/ws) with subprotocol fms-exchange-v2, Origin validation, authentication and carried operations.

transcripts.name: pace
transcripts.description: Password checks are paced: one check per second per login and per address, a check right behind the last waits for its slot, and a check that would have to wait for a second slot is turned away with rate-limited before the password is looked at. Nothing remembers a failure: there is no lockout, and the right password is evaluated as soon as its slot comes. (The server of this transcript uses an interval of 2 s and an injected clock, so the bytes do not depend on the machine.)

transcripts.name: admin-native
transcripts.description: Remote administration over TLS, using native envelopes or WebSocket binary messages as named by the transcript (DEVICE-EXCHANGE 1.4, REMOTE-ADMIN.md). Administration is off by default: admin-auth is answered admin-disabled. When turned on, clients outside allowedAddresses are closed without answer. A wrong password is bad-credentials; rapid attempts from the same client address are rate-limited by the per-address pacer; when the password verifier is saturated the answer is capacity. An authenticated session token expires after the configured lifetime (default 15 minutes) or stream close. Carries 18 operations and never host OS settings.

sealed.keys: e2e-v1.json (DEVICE-EXCHANGE vectors, 27 items DF to DP): the private key of every device named here
notes: Every box here was sealed by the generator (cmd/exchange-vectors/sealer.go) over the fixed keys of the shared vector file e2e-v1.json, with the ephemeral keys, the content keys and the nonces drawn from seeded sources: the bytes are a function of the code. The exchange server did not make, open or check any of them (item DH) - it stored and delivered them.

A `device` names a device of e2e-v1.json (`devices[].name`): that file holds its private key. A replaying product opens the `box` as a recipient of `to` with that key, with the `context` given here (the one the reader expects for the place it found the box in, never a value read from the box) and the key of `from` as the key it trusts for the sender; the result must be the `payload`.

`deviceId` is the id the transcript's server knew the device by: it is the `to` of the box's `keys` entries and the `from` of the box. Each transcript has its own server, so the same device of e2e-v1.json has another deviceId in every transcript.

A `clipboard` member names the clear text of a sealed clipboard value: the raw bytes of the transcript step that follows `clipboard-ready` are those bytes sealed under the value key of item DN (HKDF-SHA256 of the box's content key, `info` `fmsx-e2e-v1 clipboard`, in segments of 65536 with the nonce of the segment's index and last flag), and `sealedSize` and `sealedSha256` are what the server counts and answers.
